pattern.short_summary: Prior states and actions are retained as first-class records rather than discarded when superseded.
pattern.definition: Prior states and actions are retained as first-class records rather than discarded when superseded. The interface exposes them as a navigable set the user can return to, resume from, or play back in time order. History is an object in the system, not just a side effect of use.
pattern.structural_signature: Every state change appends an addressable record (a version, a modification entry, an accept/reject/edit event, a timestamped frame). The interface renders the record set as a navigable structure — a list, a stream, a timeline — and supports two operations over it: returning to a past state and continuing from there, and traversing the sequence in temporal order. Records survive the session and the same view may serve live and retrospective inspection.

dimension.category_description: How visible stages, dialogue states, histories, task decompositions, and session boundaries organize progress over time.
dimension.classification_boundary: The process structure must be exposed to users; hidden chains of model calls are excluded.
